header: Date: 2026-10-05 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Daniel Ruiz (CTO, SeaSky), Anya Petrov (ML Engineer), Marcus Lee (Product), Rachel Gomez (Security)
summary: Discovery focused on model selection across Redwood hosted/dedicated/private variants. Customer needs: multilingual support, long context (8k->32k), tool-calling for retrieval and function calls, and strict security requirements (VPC/KMS, SOC2). Discussed tradeoffs (latency vs cost), model variants (open Llama-style, Mistral-like, LLMs with tool-calling), and next steps for benchmarks and security docs.
topics: model selection (open models vs managed models)
tool-calling / function calling and external retrieval
hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
transcript:
00:00:00 - Liam Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Liam from Redwood, AE on this account. Quick intros?
00:00:10 - Daniel Ruiz: Hey Liam, Daniel here, CTO at SeaSky, we build oceanic forecasting models and are adding an LLM layer for analyst workflows.
00:00:18 - Marcus Lee: Marcus, product, focusing on how the model integrates into the UI.
00:00:22 - Anya Petrov: Anya, ML Eng, I'll be driving evals.
00:00:25 - Priya Kapoor: Priya here, Redwood solutions engineer, I'll walk through benchmarks and architecture questions.
00:00:33 - Rachel Gomez: Rachel, security, I'll be asking about compliance and keys.
00:00:40 - Liam Chen: Great, thanks. Goal for today is to understand model needs — context length, multilingual, and tool-calling — and whether hosted, dedicated, or private is a fit.
00:00:55 - Daniel Ruiz: High level — we need multilingual support (English, Spanish, Portuguese, some Japanese) for analyst notes, and the contexts can be long — most sessions are ~6k tokens but some go to 20k when aggregating logs. Ideally 8k as baseline and a path to 32k.
00:01:15 - Anya Petrov: We also need robust function/tool calling: local retrieval against internal vector DB and a set of deterministic functions for data pulls.
00:01:24 - Priya Kapoor: Got it. For context length we typically recommend testing 8k and 32k variants. Redwood supports model variants with different context windows; we can route requests to the variant that matches cost/latency needs.
00:01:38 - Marcus Lee: Quick question — when would we pick hosted vs dedicated? Cost, right?
00:01:44 - Liam Chen: It's cost and predictability. Hosted is simplest, pay-as-you-go. Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity and consistent latency under load; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives full network isolation and customer-managed keys.
00:01:58 - Rachel Gomez: On Private — is there an option for customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs?
00:02:04 - Priya Kapoor: Yes — Private supports KMS integration and HSM for key material, and we ship audit logs. We'll share the security pack with specifics.
00:02:13 - Daniel Ruiz: For model types, we're evaluating open models (like Llama-family) vs some managed offerings. We care about latency for interactive users and cost for bulk inference. How do the open models compare on Redwood?
00:02:27 - Priya Kapoor: On Redwood we profile models across latency, throughput, and quality. Open Llama-style models can be quantized and run efficiently, but for out-of-the-box tool-calling and instruction-following some families (Anthropic-style or finetuned chat models) may have better safety/formatting. We can run your prompt set through a few candidates.
00:02:46 - Anya Petrov: Are there pre-verified performance profiles? We don't want to run everything ourselves.
00:02:50 - Liam Chen: We maintain a model catalog with verified profiles — latencies at different sequence lengths, memory/kv-cache behavior, and recommended quantization. We'll share the catalog links and the profiles we run internally.
00:03:05 - Marcus Lee: Tool-calling — can the hosted API call out to our retrieval service in VPC?
00:03:12 - Priya Kapoor: Hosted can make egress calls but for strict security we recommend Dedicated with VPC peering or Private deployment so the calls stay within your network. There's also function-calling support where you can run the function locally and pass results in.
00:03:28 - Rachel Gomez: What about data retention? We can't have customer data stored in a multi-tenant cache for more than 30 days, and ideally not at all.
00:03:36 - Liam Chen: We have retention controls and can disable prefix caching for sensitive data; Dedicated and Private allow stricter retention and isolation. We'll include the retention config options in the security pack.
00:03:48 - Daniel Ruiz: On cost — can you give a rough unit cost for 8k vs 32k?
00:03:53 - Priya Kapoor: Costs scale with tokens and GPU efficiency. Roughly, a quantized 8k model on our hosted path is X per 1k tokens (we'll put exact numbers in the pricing doc), while 32k contexts can be 2-3x per token depending on kv cache and whether you can stream history. For long contexts caching/prefixing helps reduce marginal cost.
00:04:13 - Anya Petrov: We also need multilingual quality — some models degrade in Japanese. Do you have evals?
00:04:18 - Priya Kapoor: We run multilingual benchmarks; we can put your Spanish/Portuguese/Japanese prompts through candidates and show BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxies and qualitative outputs. We often recommend a finetuned or instruction-tuned variant for languages with lower base performance.
00:04:33 - Marcus Lee: What's the latency difference between 8k and 32k in practice?
00:04:38 - Priya Kapoor: For generation latencies, 32k increases both memory and per-token compute. For some kernels it's near-linear; some optimized runtimes do better. We typically see baseline latency increases ~1.5-2x for equivalent token generation length when moving from 8k to 32k on the same model family. Dedicated hardware can reduce variance.
00:04:55 - Daniel Ruiz: Can Redwood route requests dynamically to cheaper/compatible model variants?
00:05:00 - Liam Chen: Yes — smart routing policies can send traffic by latency, cost, or region. You can set fallbacks if the preferred model isn't available.
00:05:07 - Rachel Gomez: Compliance check — do you have SOC2 and ISO attestation? And pen test reports?
00:05:12 - Liam Chen: Yes, SOC2 and ISO 27001 are available; pen-test and third-party audits can be shared under NDA. We'll attach the artifacts.
00:05:20 - Anya Petrov: About function calling — how deterministic is it? If the model suggests a different function name or argument order, how do you reconcile?
00:05:27 - Priya Kapoor: We support structured function outputs; there are validation hooks and schema enforcement. If the model returns badly formatted output, we can fall back to a safe path or re-invoke with stricter decoding settings. We can show examples during a POC.
00:05:41 - Marcus Lee: Any limits on QPS for hosted versus dedicated?
00:05:45 - Priya Kapoor: Hosted has quotas and autoscaling; spikes can affect latency, but we have rate limits. Dedicated provides guaranteed throughput based on reserved GPU pools; you buy capacity units.
00:05:56 - Daniel Ruiz: For POC — we want to run a 2-week pilot: ingest 2000 analyst sessions, run retrieval+answering, compare 8k vs 32k variants on cost/latency/quality. Is that feasible?
00:06:06 - Liam Chen: Absolutely. Typical flow: we scope the dataset, pick candidate models, run automated and human evals, and then iterate. For pilot sizing we'll need the qps, prompt distribution, and retention requirements.
00:06:19 - Anya Petrov: We'll provide sample prompts and some ground truth for evaluation.
00:06:23 - Priya Kapoor: Great — we'll run them through three model candidates and return a matrix: latency, cost, quality metrics, and notes on tool-calling reliability.
00:06:33 - Daniel Ruiz: On private deployment — what's the timeline to stand up the control plane in our VPC?
00:06:38 - Priya Kapoor: For VPC Private deployments it's typically 4-6 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS integration; on-prem is longer. For Dedicated with VPC peering it's usually faster, 2-3 weeks for setup.
00:06:50 - Rachel Gomez: Do you support SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning?
00:06:53 - Liam Chen: Yes, SSO/SAML and SCIM for user provisioning, plus RBAC. We'll include the setup doc.
00:07:00 - Marcus Lee: Any gotchas we should know about when switching model families mid-rollout?
00:07:05 - Priya Kapoor: Yes — outputs, tokenization, and tool-calling behaviors can differ. We recommend canary rollouts and A/B tests, and Redwood supports automatic fallback policies and per-route model bindings.
00:07:17 - Daniel Ruiz: For benchmarks, we care about end-to-end latency including retrieval. Can you instrument the retrieval step?
00:07:23 - Priya Kapoor: Yes — Redwood Console gives per-route breakdowns including time spent in pre-processing, retrieval, model inference, and post-processing. We can surface token-level cost too.
00:07:35 - Anya Petrov: Any example customers in adjacent domains?
00:07:38 - Liam Chen: We have customers in maritime analytics and energy who do long-context retrieval and multilingual support; we'll anonymize references.
00:07:45 - Marcus Lee: Ok next steps?
00:07:47 - Liam Chen: Recap — we'll: 1) send pricing + model catalog, 2) share security pack (SOC2/ISO/KMS/HSM details), 3) Priya will run the first benchmark on your sample prompts (8k vs 32k) and share results by Oct 12, 4) schedule POC scoping next week with your infra and security teams.
00:08:06 - Rachel Gomez: We'll send the list of security contacts and legal for NDA.
00:08:10 - Daniel Ruiz: Sounds good. Any final questions?
00:08:14 - Priya Kapoor: One clarifying Q — for the 32k contexts, do you need full persistent history for every session or can some older tokens be offloaded to external retrieval?
00:08:24 - Anya Petrov: We can offload older logs to retrieval in many cases but for some analyst sessions we prefer true 32k context for a single-turn summary.
00:08:33 - Priya Kapoor: That helps; we can show hybrid patterns where prefix caching + retrieval reduces cost but preserves quality for the critical window.
00:08:41 - Liam Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and benchmark plan.
00:08:46 - Daniel Ruiz: Thank you.
00:08:48 - Marcus Lee: Thanks all.
00:08:50 - (call ended)

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription idiosyncrasies; names and product names occasionally fuzzed. References: security pack link (shared post-call), model catalog link (redwood.com/models), pricing spreadsheet (shared).
